# bugs #3153: Multiple definition of line labels at link time with --debug for static functions defined in a header

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3153/
- Category: [Analyzed, not fixed](../../unresolved.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Keep open for static functions in headers. r12010 fixed the reported case of an inline function without static.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17176 the files attached to the ticket compile and link with `--debug` without a
`Multiple definition` error. The case that the ticket's comments leave open still fails. When the
function in the header is declared `static inline`, or `static` without `inline`, and two source
files include the header, the linker reports
`?ASlink-Error-Multiple definition of C$inline.h$16$1_0$2` and the same error for the other lines
of the function. sdcc exits with 1.

Both results were reproduced for mcs51 with the small and large models, each with and without
`--stack-auto`, and for z80. The test used the ticket's files with a definition of the array,
which the attachment does not have. For mcs51 the array is declared `__xdata`. No other port was
tried.

## Known

[r12010](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/12010/) fixed the case of a function that is declared
`inline` without `static`. It sets a flag on the iCodes that sdcc creates when it expands a
function inline, and `cdbWriteCLine` in `src/cdbFile.c` and `dwWriteCLine` in `src/SDCCdwarf2.c`
write no line label for iCodes that have the flag. In the thirteenth comment a maintainer
announces the revision and says that it does not cover `static inline`.

`createFunction` in `src/SDCCast.c` generates code for every `static inline` function, so each
module that includes the header contains the function itself. `cdbWriteCLine` builds the name of
each line label from the base name of the source file, the line, the level, and the block number.
The name does not identify the module. `mcs51_emitDebuggerSymbol` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` defines the
label with `==.`, which makes it a global symbol, and `z80_emitDebuggerSymbol` declares it global
too. Two modules that have code for one line of a header therefore define the same global symbol.
Inlining is not needed for this. A `static` function that is not inline gives the same errors.

## Open

The linker writes one `L:C$...` record with one address for each of these names to the `.cdb`
file, and sdcdb reads the records in `parseLnkRec` in `debugger/mcs51/symtab.c`. The open
question is how the debug information represents a header line whose code exists in several
modules. No patch was written.

## Related

In the fourth comment the reporter names bug #2591 as similar. That ticket is closed.
